samples.question: This picture shows one bordered panel of 21 rows and 21 columns of square cells. Every cell is a flat block of exactly one of two tones, dark or pale, and both tones appear many times inside the panel. Nine different symbols have been interleaved cell by cell across the whole panel, so the panel on its own looks like clutter and no symbol is drawn anywhere in one piece. Two solid triangles are drawn in the margins outside the panel, far apart from each other: one of them lies beyond the left or the right side of the panel and points sideways at a panel row, and the other lies above or below the panel and points at a panel column. Each triangle points at exactly one panel row or one panel column, and the two triangles are always far apart. A few small clutter bars are also scattered on the background; they are plain rectangles, they never taper to a point, and they carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Take the row the sideways triangle points at, and keep that row together with every third row from it, counting both upwards and downwards - seven rows in all. Take the column the other triangle points at, and keep that column together with every third column from it, counting both leftwards and rightwards - seven columns in all. Discard every other row and column, close up the gaps, and read the 49 surviving cells as a 7-row, 7-column picture in their original order. The dark cells of that picture form exactly one of nine symbols on the 7 by 7 grid. 'plus' is the full middle row together with the full middle column. 'ex' is the two full diagonals. 'ring' is a hollow rectangle outline five cells wide and seven cells tall, set one cell in from the left and right edges. 'tee' is the full top row together with the full middle column. 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. 'zee' is the full top row and the full bottom row joined by a diagonal that climbs from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. 'arrow' is the full middle column with a splayed head on the top four rows: one cell out on each side in the second row, two cells out in the third row, three cells out in the fourth row. 'vee' is two thick diagonals that start at the two top corners, step one column inwards every two rows, and meet at the single middle cell of the bottom row. 'corners' is a two-by-two block in each of the four corners together with three side-by-side cells at the very centre. A few cells of the panel are speckle: the surviving picture can differ from its symbol in a small number of cells, so choose the symbol it is closest to, cell by cell. Neither triangle settles the answer on its own, because each of the nine interleaved sub-lattices carries a different one of the nine symbols: the sideways triangle alone leaves three symbols possible and the other triangle alone leaves a different three, so both distant pointers and the whole panel must be used. Which symbol do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, corners, ell, ex, plus, ring, tee, vee, zee.
